q:
Started sleeping through the night at 6 weeks (9-11 hour stretches with no wake ups/feeds.) 

For the past 1-2 months, no longer getting those long stretches.
x: Mother of an exclusively breastfed 5-month-old who has always nursed to sleep.

q: Open to gentle sleep training (not CIO.) I am willing to let her fuss for a bit, the issue is that she immediately starts screaming as soon as she wakes up so she’s already past fussing.
x: Same mother on why gentle methods do not fit her baby.

q: I need to grow a pair and put him to bed awake. I didn’t realize the “drowsy but awake” thing was for newborns only. Thank you for your advice. I’m just gonna pick a hell week sometime in May and ride it out. 😩 It’s gonna be so hard but it has to be done.
x: Parent of a 6-month-old with repeated wakes in the first hours, after one reply.

q: I place him down awake in his crib and set a timer he just screams. I know I need to push through it but last time I tried he cried  until he threw up.
x: Parent of an 11.5-month-old Ferber-trained once, now untrained.

q: I have 2 trips this summer and I don’t want to set him up for failure . Also, I want my naps and early evenings back .
x: Same parent on why now.

x: Parent of a 7.5-month-old nap-trained with the chair method.

q:
He makes her drowsy then puts her down, no crying. My nanny and mom do the same, no crying. 

Yet for me - she screams?
x: Same parent; the husband, nanny and grandmother can all put her down.

q: I prefer to put her down drowsy but don’t understand why she resists so much when it’s me
x: Same parent.

q: It makes me feel like the work I’ve put in for him to be on a schedule is worthless and all of it is based on “luck”.

q: Sometimes it feels like they want me to say I’m struggling and so tired and miserable.

q: We did Ferber a few months ago and she was stubborn but it ended up working pretty good.
x: Breastfeeding mother of an 11-month-old who still wakes once between 12 and 2.

q: Last night I tried doing Ferber check ins at the wake. It went on for an hour and eventually I just fed her and she slept for another 5 hours after that.
x: Same mother.

q: I get frustrated that the wakes are habit and not genuine hunger or thirst and I am so freaking tired from not having a long sleep the past 11 months.
x: Same mother.

q: Could it still get better at this point? Or is this not the right sleep training style for our baby?

q: Did it resolve on its own or was there something that actually helped? I will try anything.
x: Same parent.

x: Title of a post by the parent of a 3-month-old.

x: Couple with a 4.5-month-old who contact naps; bedtime is the problem.

x: Same parent.

q: i believe it’s me who can’t figure this sleep stuff out. im really struggling with the math, and could use some help.
x: Same parent closes the post.

q: i studied my son’s wake windows HARD today, capped daytime sleep at 3.5 hours after a 6:30am wake. put baby down after a final wake window of 2.20 and voila… no crying. put himself to bed in 15 minutes. i could cry i’m so thrilled.
x: Same parent two days later on one commenter's numbers.

q: We’ve landed on the Ferber method, but I still feel so guilty. I feel sick even thinking about letting baby just… Cry.
x: Mother of a 9-month-old who has coslept and contact napped, deciding to train.

x: Same mother.

q: any advice for the Ferber method? I plan on ordering the book soon.

x: Same mother on what pushed her decision.

q:
Baby’s associations/anxiety honestly had me questioning the entire thing. I felt \*so awful\* that my own son was scared of his bedroom.

I am really glad to say that it did improve. It took a couple weeks, but it gradually improved.
